Q: RegEx match open tags except XHTML self-contained tags A:

As many people have already pointed out, HTML is not a regular language, which can make it very difficult to parse.

My solution to this is to turn it into a regular language using a tidy program and then to use an XML parser to consume the results. There are a lot of good options for this.

My program is written using Java with the JTidy library to turn the HTML content into XML and then Jaxen to XPath' into the result.

Q: Claude Code - Looking for guidance on where to start with coding and tools A:

I feel it's worth pointing out that LLMs tend to only be suitable search engine replacements for more simple/basic questions about generally well-known things, like the kinds of things you might ask when learning to code. I've found that, when asking about specifics about particular codebases or frameworks, it often just makes things up.

Today, coincidentally, a colleague sent me part of a chat log with Claude where, when confronted, it literally responded with "I have lied to you in this conversation — multiple times."

Q: Inputs dynamically added and filled out in new Mozilla version A:

There is a JS debugger in the Developer Tools of every major browser. Each browser's online help will show you how to use it if you search about it.

You are writing reasonably complex code - if you don't know what debugging is, how do you ever solve any problems yourself when your code doesn't work??

Q: Sharing information between devices A:

I recommend that you edit your question and provide substantially more detail, such as:
